title: Profile Drift Detector and Heuristic Bitwidth Fallback for AWQ/GPTQ Experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a lightweight production-facing detector that flags quantization profile drift and triggers a heuristic bitwidth fallback policy for AWQ/GPTQ conversions. This ticket covers design and prototype of (1) a streaming profile-drift detector that works on sample traffic cohorts, (2) a per-route fallback heuristic that selects int8/int4 rollback targets based on calibrated quality thresholds, and (3) integration points with the eval harness and rollout automation. We purposefully focus on a low-latency, low-cost detector that uses summary statistics (perplexity delta, entropy shift, top-token distribution drift) rather than running full evals for every change.
acceptance_criteria: A streaming detector computes per-cohort drift score within 60s of new traffic and persists 30-day rolling summaries.
Detector flags map to automated fallback actions: for high drift -> rollback to int8 profile; for medium drift -> trigger full eval job and cautionary alert.
Fallback decision respects per-route fidelity budgets and does not exceed configured daily rollback budget.
End-to-end test demonstrates AWQ->GPTQ converted model with introduced quant noise being automatically mitigated by the fallback in a staged rollout (canary -> 10% -> 100%).
Dashboard tile shows detector metrics (drift_score, p99 latency of detection, last_action) and historical toggles for audits.
tasks: Design drift scoring function and normalization (entropy delta + token distribution Wasserstein component).
Prototype streaming collector that computes per-cohort summaries (30s windows) and persists to metrics backend.
Implement heuristic fallback policy (int4->int8 -> AWQ->GPTQ variant) and safe-guards (daily budget, cooldowns).
Wire detector alarms to rollout automation and add audit trails in console logs.
Create focused eval suite with 200 prompt/response pairs for semantic and instruction-following checks to validate flagged cases.
Create dashboard and runbook describing operator actions and incident steps.
notes: We intentionally avoid running heavy evals on every config push. Instead we use a two-stage approach: quick statistical screening (this detector) followed by targeted eval jobs only when the detector crosses the medium/high thresholds. The heuristic fallback is conservative: prefer higher-bitwidth profiles first and only escalate to full rollback if the targeted eval confirms regression.
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete - built prototype collector that emits entropy and top-token histograms to metrics. Initial false-positive rate ~12% on held-out shuffle traffic (acceptable).

2026-03-08: Implemented per-route budget enforcement in rollout automation; added cooldown period (2 hours) after fallback action to prevent flapping.
2026-03-10: Integration test passed for canary scenario using AWQ-int4->AWQ-int8 fallback; raised follow-up to add GPTQ variant comparisons.
